sec: 1°/2°/3° differentiation and radiological bone changes · p880

items.q: PTH levels — 1) 1°  2) 2°  3) 3° … A) 500-1000 pg/ml  B) >1000 pg/ml  C) >50 pg/ml
Sr. Ca/PO4 — 1) 1°  2) 2°  3) 3° … A) Ca↓ PO4↑  B) Ca↑↑ PO4↑↑  C) Ca↑ PO4↓
items.exp: 1° Ca↑ PO4↓; 2° Ca↓ PO4↑; 3° Ca↑↑ PO4↑↑. (Book p880)

items.q: Cause — 1) 1°  2) 2°  3) 3° … A) Seen in CKD  B) Long-standing CKD  C) Adenoma (m/c) / hyperplasia (MEN 1/2A)
items.exp: 1° adenoma (m/c)/hyperplasia MEN 1/2A; 2° CKD; 3° long-standing CKD. (Book p880)

items.q: The MOST characteristic bone change of hyperparathyroidism is:
opts: Subperiosteal resorption, radial side of proximal/middle phalanx of index and middle finger
Acral osteolysis of the distal phalanges
items.exp: Subperiosteal resorption, radial side of proximal or middle phalanx of index and middle finger — most characteristic. (Book p880)

items.q: The most common (m/c) bone change in hyperparathyroidism is:
items.exp: Diffuse bone resorption is m/c. (Book p880)
Rugger jersey spine = intercortical bone resorption. (Book p880)

items.q: Book-listed radiological bone changes include diffuse resorption, rugger jersey spine, brown tumor, salt-and-pepper skull, endosteal scalloping and acral osteolysis. Pick the ODD ONE OUT:
items.exp: Listed: 1–6 as above; ground-glass matrix is not among them. (Book p880)

items.q: The number of radiological bone changes listed in the book (diffuse resorption to osteitis fibrosa cystica) is:
items.exp: Seven: diffuse resorption, rugger jersey spine, brown tumor, salt-and-pepper skull, endosteal scalloping, acral osteolysis, osteitis fibrosa cystica. (Book p880)
